official.deadline_note: Questions on the proposal process had to be sent by 8 October 2026, with queries and responses published on the announcement page; funding decisions are targeted for 9 November 2026.
official.application_cycle: Third phase of SA-TIED, launched 17 September 2026
official.status_note: The call was launched on 17 September 2026 and closes on 15 October 2026 at 23:59 (UTC+2); as at the verification date of 10 October 2026 the submission forms on the announcement page remain open.
official.funding_period: one-off honorarium on delivery of a working paper
benefits: Research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000 paid upon delivery of a working paper, depending on the qualifications of the lead researcher and assessment of the proposal
Publication of papers that pass initial screening under UNU-WIDER copyright as an SA-TIED research paper, and possibly in the WIDER Working Paper Series
A small travel stipend for researchers using the South African tax administrative data living outside of Gauteng
Participation in at least one knowledge-sharing event and engagement with the SA-TIED communications team on a knowledge mobilization output such as a video, infographic, brief or blog
Inclusion in a research team building capacity in South African institutions, with UNU-WIDER seeking participation from Historically Disadvantaged Institutions
eligibility: Proposals from individuals, groups of individuals, and non-profit organizations are welcome
The call invites South Africa-based and international researchers; applications from women and South African researchers are particularly encouraged
Special consideration for research teams that include junior and early-career researchers as well as scholars from the Global South
Research must be conducted primarily, but not exclusively, using South African tax administrative data
Papers must be written in English and limited to 10,000 words or fewer, inclusive of text, tables, figures, footnotes and references
Papers may use either theoretical or empirical approaches
requirements: Proposals must be submitted electronically using the online form on the RfRP announcement page - three forms exist: one for individuals, one for groups of individuals, and one for non-profit organizations
Details such as address, gender, nationality and date of birth of all researchers involved must be entered on the form
The cover page, the proposal, and short CVs of five pages or less per researcher must be uploaded
The provided proposal template must be used for the proposal
documents: Proposal prepared on the provided template (10,000 words or fewer, in English)
Short CV of five pages or less for each researcher involved
Contact and personal details (address, gender, nationality, date of birth) for every researcher entered on the form
selection_criteria: Each proposal is reviewed for scientific merit and feasibility
Proposals are selected on three criteria: (i) relevance to the research project, (ii) strength of empirical and policy contributions, and (iii) qualifications and experience of the research team
Preference is given to applications from early-career and female scholars, as well as researchers from South Africa
UNU-WIDER seeks to include researchers from a broad range of South African institutions, particularly Historically Disadvantaged Institutions
coverage: Total research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000, paid upon delivery of a working paper; the deliverable must be deemed acceptable by UNU-WIDER before payment is made
The honorarium is expected to cover all expenses associated with the conduct of the proposed research, including data collection and research assistance
A small travel stipend is available for researchers using the South African tax administrative data living outside of Gauteng
application_method: Download the Request for Research Proposals document and the proposal template from the announcement page
Prepare the proposal on the provided template, within the 10,000-word limit, in English
Select the correct online form - individual, group of individuals, or non-profit organization
Enter the contact details and the details of all researchers involved, including address, gender, nationality and date of birth
Upload the cover page, the proposal and short CVs of five pages or less per researcher
Submit the form before 15 October 2026 at 23:59 (UTC+2)
official.application_route: Electronic submission only, through the individual, group or NGO online form on the RfRP announcement page, with the cover page, templated proposal and CVs uploaded.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to South Africa-based and international researchers; no citizenship restriction is published. Applications from South African researchers are particularly encouraged.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the call explicitly invites both South Africa-based and international researchers, with special consideration for scholars from the Global South
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must fit the workstreams on public revenue mobilisation for inclusive development (WS2) and poverty, inequality, and labour markets (WS3), and be conducted primarily, but not exclusively, using South African tax administrative data
official.research_requirement: The deliverable is a policy-oriented working paper of 10,000 words or fewer using South African tax administrative data; no budget is required and the proposal must follow the published template
official.duration: Milestone-driven: first drafts due 8 June 2027, a work-in-progress workshop in June/July 2027, and final drafts due 8 September 2027, with knowledge-sharing events planned subsequently
official.description: The United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER), together with the National Treasury of South Africa, is requesting research proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme on public revenue mobilization and poverty, inequality, and labour markets, using South African tax administrative data. Papers that pass screening are published as SA-TIED research papers under UNU-WIDER copyright, and successful researchers sign a consultant contract or institutional agreement with UNU-WIDER.
official.program_type: Research grant / commissioned research honorarium (not a degree scholarship)
official.english_requirement: Working papers need to be written in English (10,000 words or fewer, inclusive of text, tables, figures, footnotes and references)

applicant_utility.summary: This is commissioned research, not a scholarship: you are paid an honorarium of US$3,000-10,000 for delivering an acceptable working paper, and the money is explicitly expected to absorb every research cost, so there is no tuition, living stipend or fee support attached. The call closes at 23:59 UTC+2 on 15 October 2026 - five days from the verification date - and submission is only through one of three online forms (individual, group, or non-profit), so pick the right form type before you start typing. Scope tightly to the two workstreams and to South African tax administrative data, because relevance to the project is the first of the three published selection criteria and only the final decision is ever communicated - expect no feedback if you are not selected.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Economists and social scientists - especially early-career, female and South Africa-based researchers - who can deliver a publishable 10,000-word policy paper using tax administrative data within the June-September 2027 draft cycle.
application_readiness_checklist: Choose the correct submission form first: individual, group of individuals, or non-profit organization
Download and use the published proposal template - off-template proposals risk screening problems
Cast the proposal explicitly against the WS2 revenue-mobilization or WS3 poverty/inequality/labour-market questions and the tax-data angle
Prepare a five-page-or-less CV for every researcher on the team, plus the cover page, before opening the form
Enter each researcher's address, gender, nationality and date of birth accurately - the form demands these details
Submit before 23:59 UTC+2 on 15 October 2026; no budget document is needed
common_rejection_risks: A proposal that reads as general development economics rather than the two named workstreams - relevance is criterion one
Overrunning the 10,000-word limit or ignoring the template
Using the wrong form type for your team structure (individual vs group vs non-profit)
Submitting after 23:59 UTC+2 on 15 October 2026, or expecting feedback - only the accept/decline decision is communicated
A weak CV trail relative to the honorarium band sought, since qualifications of the lead researcher drive the amount offered
Proposing data access plans that ignore the confidentiality restrictions National Treasury attaches to tax administrative datasets
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The honorarium is expected to cover all research expenses including data collection and research assistance; there is no living-cost, tuition or salary support in this award, and only non-Gauteng researchers using the tax data can receive the small travel stipend.
document_audit: Short CVs must be five pages or less per researcher - trim before uploading rather than hoping for leniency
All researchers' personal details (address, gender, nationality, date of birth) must be on the form, so collect them from co-authors before you start
No budget document is required - spending time on one is wasted effort

Successful teams will later sign a consultant contract or institutional contractual agreement under UNU conditions of service, and copyright transfers to UNU-WIDER unless no further publication is expected
alerts: The call closed five days after the verification date - treat 15 October 2026, 23:59 UTC+2 as hard
Questions on the proposal process closed on 8 October 2026; check the announcement page for published query responses rather than emailing late
Funding decisions are targeted for 9 November 2026, first drafts are due 8 June 2027 and final drafts 8 September 2027 - the schedule after award is demanding
Administrative and academic support is available for researchers needing help submitting (requests to the SA-TIED support address published on the page)
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Electronic submission via the individual, group or NGO form on the announcement page with cover page, templated proposal and CVs uploaded; eligibility and merit screening by UNU-WIDER, decisions targeted for 9 November 2026, then consultant contract and milestone-based paper delivery.
